sentence: Which conclusion accurately limits the claim about flexible hours?
setupText: After a company introduced flexible hours, staff reported less stress. The same month, workloads also fell. No separate effects were measured.
taskText: Which conclusion accurately limits the claim about flexible hours?
text: After a company introduced flexible hours, staff reported less stress. The same month, workloads also fell. No separate effects were measured. Which conclusion accurately limits the claim about flexible hours?
options: Flexible hours may have contributed to lower reported stress.
Flexible hours reduced stress more than the lighter workloads did.
The lighter workloads probably explain most of the reduction in stress.
Flexible hours had no effect once workloads were reduced.
answer: Flexible hours may have contributed to lower reported stress.
explanation: 'May have contributed' allows a role for flexible hours without separating it from the workload change.

rationales.Flexible hours reduced stress more than: No separate effects were measured, so their relative contributions cannot be ranked.
rationales.The lighter workloads probably explain m: This favors one explanation without evidence about its contribution.
rationales.Flexible hours had no effect once worklo: The simultaneous changes do not show that flexible hours had no effect.
rationales.Flexible hours may have contributed to l: 'May have contributed' allows a role for flexible hours without separating it from the workload change.

sentence: Which paraphrase places the uncertainty on the interpretation?
setupText: An editor writes, 'The figures appear to support the proposal.' The figures have been checked, but their implications remain debatable.
taskText: Which paraphrase places the uncertainty on the interpretation?
text: An editor writes, 'The figures appear to support the proposal.' The figures have been checked, but their implications remain debatable. Which paraphrase places the uncertainty on the interpretation?
options: The proposal has tentative support from the figures.
The figures themselves may not have been checked adequately.
The figures show that the proposal has already been adopted.
The proposal is supported by figures that are probably inaccurate.
answer: The proposal has tentative support from the figures.
focusKey: coverage-hedging-and-precision-b2-1622:Locating uncertainty in interpretation rather than data
explanation: 'Tentative support' means the figures are provisionally interpreted as favouring the proposal, but that conclusion remains open to revision. The qualification concerns their significance, not whether the numbers were checked.

rationales.The figures themselves may not have been: This moves uncertainty to data checking, which the context says is complete.
rationales.The proposal has tentative support from: 'Tentative support' means the figures are provisionally interpreted as favouring the proposal, but that conclusion remains open to revision. The qualification concerns their significance, not whether the numbers were checked.
rationales.The figures show that the proposal has a: Support for a proposal does not establish an adoption decision.
rationales.The proposal is supported by figures tha: This invents a concern about numerical accuracy rather than interpretation.

sentence: Which wording gives the reported percentage with the correct group?
setupText: A housing survey received replies from 300 tenants out of 1,000 contacted. Of those who replied, 60% favored longer leases.
taskText: Which wording gives the reported percentage with the correct group?
text: A housing survey received replies from 300 tenants out of 1,000 contacted. Of those who replied, 60% favored longer leases. Which wording gives the reported percentage with the correct group?
options: Sixty percent of all tenants contacted favored longer leases.
Sixty percent of local tenants are likely to favor longer leases.
Sixty percent of tenants who favored longer leases replied.
Sixty percent of respondents favored longer leases.
answer: Sixty percent of respondents favored longer leases.
explanation: 'Respondents' names the 300 people whose answers produced the percentage.

rationales.Sixty percent of all tenants contacted f: The percentage describes respondents, not the full 1,000 contacted.
rationales.Sixty percent of local tenants are likel: This extends the result to a wider population and adds a prediction.
rationales.Sixty percent of respondents favored lon: 'Respondents' names the 300 people whose answers produced the percentage.
rationales.Sixty percent of tenants who favored lon: This reverses the groups: the survey reports preferences among replies, not reply rates among supporters.

sentence: Which summary preserves the condition?
setupText: A supplier writes, 'We can deliver by Friday, provided payment clears by Tuesday.'
taskText: Which summary preserves the condition?
text: A supplier writes, 'We can deliver by Friday, provided payment clears by Tuesday.' Which summary preserves the condition?
options: Payment clearing by Tuesday is expected because delivery is on Friday.
Friday delivery depends on payment clearing by Tuesday.
Friday delivery is likely even if payment clears after Tuesday.
Payment may clear on Tuesday, so delivery has been confirmed for Friday.
answer: Friday delivery depends on payment clearing by Tuesday.
focusKey: coverage-hedging-and-precision-b2-1624:Provided as a condition on a commitment
explanation: 'Provided' makes Friday delivery conditional on payment clearing by Tuesday. 'Depends on' preserves that requirement rather than announcing an unconditional delivery date.

rationales.Friday delivery depends on payment clear: 'Provided' makes Friday delivery conditional on payment clearing by Tuesday. 'Depends on' preserves that requirement rather than announcing an unconditional delivery date.
rationales.Payment clearing by Tuesday is expected: This reverses the relationship and treats the delivery as settled.
rationales.Friday delivery is likely even if paymen: The supplier makes no claim about delivery when the condition fails.
rationales.Payment may clear on Tuesday, so deliver: A possible payment event does not establish that the condition has been met.

sentence: What does 'plausible' mean in this context?
setupText: A reviewer writes, 'The explanation is plausible, but the available evidence does not favor it over the alternatives.'
taskText: What does 'plausible' mean in this context?
text: A reviewer writes, 'The explanation is plausible, but the available evidence does not favor it over the alternatives.' What does 'plausible' mean in this context?
options: It is the explanation the evidence favors most.
It is the explanation the reviewer has accepted as correct.
It can reasonably be considered as a possible explanation.
It requires less evidence than the alternatives to be accepted.
answer: It can reasonably be considered as a possible explanation.
explanation: 'Plausible' makes the explanation credible enough to consider without ranking it as most likely.

rationales.It is the explanation the evidence favor: The second clause explicitly says it is not favored over the alternatives.
rationales.It can reasonably be considered as a pos: 'Plausible' makes the explanation credible enough to consider without ranking it as most likely.
rationales.It is the explanation the reviewer has a: The reviewer leaves the competing explanations open.
rationales.It requires less evidence than the alter: Plausibility does not establish a lower standard of evidence.

sentence: Which sentence preserves the stage and scope of the evidence?
setupText: A pilot involved ten volunteers. Eight liked the new booking system. The report is meant to describe this early feedback.
taskText: Which sentence preserves the stage and scope of the evidence?
text: A pilot involved ten volunteers. Eight liked the new booking system. The report is meant to describe this early feedback. Which sentence preserves the stage and scope of the evidence?
options: Customers generally prefer the new booking system.
The booking system has been shown to improve customer satisfaction.
Initial feedback from the volunteers was mostly positive.
The pilot suggests the system should replace the existing service.
answer: Initial feedback from the volunteers was mostly positive.
explanation: 'Initial' marks the early stage, 'volunteers' keeps the group, and 'mostly' fits eight of ten.

rationales.Customers generally prefer the new booki: Ten volunteers cannot establish customers' general preference.
rationales.The booking system has been shown to imp: Liking a system in a small pilot does not establish a measured improvement.
rationales.Initial feedback from the volunteers was: 'Initial' marks the early stage, 'volunteers' keeps the group, and 'mostly' fits eight of ten.
rationales.The pilot suggests the system should rep: This moves from reporting feedback to a replacement recommendation that was not requested.

sentence: Which interpretation keeps the degree of success?
setupText: A manager says, 'The revised process largely addresses the delays, although two bottlenecks remain.'
taskText: Which interpretation keeps the degree of success?
text: A manager says, 'The revised process largely addresses the delays, although two bottlenecks remain.' Which interpretation keeps the degree of success?
options: The revised process mainly concerns delays rather than costs.
The revised process offers little help with the delays.
The two remaining bottlenecks have become less important.
The revised process deals with much of the delay problem.
answer: The revised process deals with much of the delay problem.
explanation: 'Much of' captures substantial but incomplete progress, consistent with remaining bottlenecks.

rationales.The revised process mainly concerns dela: This changes 'largely addresses' into a statement about subject matter.
rationales.The revised process offers little help w: 'Largely' indicates substantial success, not little help.
rationales.The two remaining bottlenecks have becom: The sentence says they remain but does not assess their importance.
rationales.The revised process deals with much of t: 'Much of' captures substantial but incomplete progress, consistent with remaining bottlenecks.

sentence: Which wording keeps the forecast attributed?
setupText: A newspaper reports that the operator expects fares to rise. The newspaper has not independently checked the operator's forecast.
taskText: Which wording keeps the forecast attributed?
text: A newspaper reports that the operator expects fares to rise. The newspaper has not independently checked the operator's forecast. Which wording keeps the forecast attributed?
options: Fares are rising, the newspaper has confirmed.
The newspaper expects fares to rise.
The operator has decided how much fares will rise.
The operator expects fares to rise.
answer: The operator expects fares to rise.
explanation: Making 'the operator' the subject of 'expects' assigns the forecast to that source. It does not claim that the newspaper verified a future increase.

Making 'the operator' the subject of 'expects' assigns the forecast to that source. It does not claim that the newspaper verified a future increase.
rationales.Fares are rising, the newspaper has conf: This changes a forecast into a current change and invents independent confirmation.
This transfers the expectation from the operator to the newspaper.
rationales.The operator has decided how much fares: Expecting an increase does not establish a decision about its size.

sentence: Which revision is clearest?
setupText: A draft says, 'The new layout might possibly perhaps reduce queues.' The writer wants one ordinary hedge for possibility, with no change in confidence.
taskText: Which revision is clearest?
text: A draft says, 'The new layout might possibly perhaps reduce queues.' The writer wants one ordinary hedge for possibility, with no change in confidence. Which revision is clearest?
options: The new layout is likely to reduce queues.
The new layout should substantially reduce queues.
The new layout is unlikely to reduce queues.
The new layout might reduce queues.
answer: The new layout might reduce queues.
focusKey: coverage-hedging-and-precision-b2-1629:Removing redundant hedges without strengthening the claim
explanation: One 'might' expresses the intended possibility without stacking similar hedges.

rationales.The new layout is likely to reduce queue: 'Likely' makes success probable, stronger than the requested possibility.
One 'might' expresses the intended possibility without stacking similar hedges.
rationales.The new layout should substantially redu: This adds an expectation of success and a large effect.
rationales.The new layout is unlikely to reduce que: This introduces a negative prediction absent from the draft.

sentence: Which paraphrase keeps the probability judgment?
setupText: A report says, 'The change is unlikely to affect current customers.'
taskText: Which paraphrase keeps the probability judgment?
text: A report says, 'The change is unlikely to affect current customers.' Which paraphrase keeps the probability judgment?
options: The change is not expected to affect current customers.
The effect on current customers has not been investigated.
The change could affect current customers quite substantially.
The change has had little effect on current customers.
answer: The change is not expected to affect current customers.
explanation: 'Not expected to' preserves the prediction of no effect while leaving some possibility open.

rationales.The effect on current customers has not: Unlikelihood is a probability judgment, not a statement that no investigation occurred.
rationales.The change could affect current customer: This introduces magnitude and does not preserve the low-probability judgment.
rationales.The change is not expected to affect cur: 'Not expected to' preserves the prediction of no effect while leaving some possibility open.
rationales.The change has had little effect on curr: This reports a past or present observed effect rather than a forecast.

sentence: Which conclusion stays within the stated limitation?
setupText: An engineer writes, 'Under normal operating conditions, the battery lasts eight hours.'
taskText: Which conclusion stays within the stated limitation?
text: An engineer writes, 'Under normal operating conditions, the battery lasts eight hours.' Which conclusion stays within the stated limitation?
options: Eight hours is the battery's minimum life in cold conditions.
The eight-hour figure applies to normal operating conditions.
Most users will get exactly eight hours of use.
The battery's life is uncertain under normal conditions.
answer: The eight-hour figure applies to normal operating conditions.
focusKey: coverage-hedging-and-precision-b2-1631:Conditions as the scope of a performance figure
explanation: 'Under normal operating conditions' limits the circumstances to which the eight-hour claim applies. It does not express doubt about the result within those circumstances.

rationales.Eight hours is the battery's minimum lif: The statement does not cover cold conditions or specify a minimum.
rationales.Most users will get exactly eight hours: Operating conditions do not establish a user proportion or exact individual duration.
rationales.The battery's life is uncertain under no: The writer gives a result under those conditions rather than expressing uncertainty about it.
rationales.The eight-hour figure applies to normal: 'Under normal operating conditions' limits the circumstances to which the eight-hour claim applies. It does not express doubt about the result within those circumstances.

sentence: Which sentence does so precisely?
setupText: The survey response rate rose from 40% to 45%. A writer wants to name the difference in percentage points.
taskText: Which sentence does so precisely?
text: The survey response rate rose from 40% to 45%. A writer wants to name the difference in percentage points. Which sentence does so precisely?
options: The response rate rose by five percent.
The response rate rose by five percentage points.
The response rate rose to five percentage points.
The response rate rose by forty-five percentage points.
answer: The response rate rose by five percentage points.
explanation: The difference between 40% and 45% is five percentage points.

rationales.The response rate rose by five percentag: The difference between 40% and 45% is five percentage points.
A five-percent relative rise from 40% would give 42%, not 45%.
rationales.The response rate rose to five percentag: 'To' names the final value, but the final response rate is 45%.
rationales.The response rate rose by forty-five per: Forty-five percent is the final rate, not the size of the increase.

sentence: Which summary identifies the stated reason readers may be misled, without alleging false figures or deliberate deception?
setupText: A review says, 'The article is somewhat misleading: its figures are correct, but the headline leaves out the date range.'
taskText: Which summary identifies the stated reason readers may be misled, without alleging false figures or deliberate deception?
text: A review says, 'The article is somewhat misleading: its figures are correct, but the headline leaves out the date range.' Which summary identifies the stated reason readers may be misled, without alleging false figures or deliberate deception?
options: The article's figures are probably inaccurate.
The article deliberately hides a fall in performance.
The article may mislead readers because its headline lacks the date range.
The article would be accurate if its figures were updated.
answer: The article may mislead readers because its headline lacks the date range.
explanation: The missing date range is the specified source of possible misunderstanding. Accurate figures do not prevent a headline from giving readers an incomplete impression.

rationales.The article's figures are probably inacc: The review explicitly accepts the figures as correct.
rationales.The article may mislead readers because: The missing date range is the specified source of possible misunderstanding. Accurate figures do not prevent a headline from giving readers an incomplete impression.
rationales.The article deliberately hides a fall in: The review does not establish intent or a fall in performance.
rationales.The article would be accurate if its fig: The stated problem is the missing date range in the headline, not outdated figures.

sentence: Which revision fits?
setupText: A report states, 'To date, no customers have complained about the update.' The writer wants to preserve the time boundary.
taskText: Which revision fits?
text: A report states, 'To date, no customers have complained about the update.' The writer wants to preserve the time boundary. Which revision fits?
options: Customers are unlikely to complain about the update.
No customer complaints about the update have been received so far.
The update has prevented complaints from customers.
Customers who complained before the update are now satisfied.
answer: No customer complaints about the update have been received so far.
focusKey: coverage-hedging-and-precision-b2-1634:To date as a provisional time boundary
explanation: 'So far' keeps the record limited to the period ending now.

rationales.Customers are unlikely to complain about: This turns a past-to-present record into a prediction.
rationales.The update has prevented complaints from: The absence of complaints does not show that the update prevented them.
rationales.No customer complaints about the update: 'So far' keeps the record limited to the period ending now.
rationales.Customers who complained before the upda: The report provides no comparison with earlier complainants or their satisfaction.

sentence: Which paraphrase keeps the stated precision?
setupText: An analyst says, 'The estimate is in the region of $12,000.' No tighter range is available.
taskText: Which paraphrase keeps the stated precision?
text: An analyst says, 'The estimate is in the region of $12,000.' No tighter range is available. Which paraphrase keeps the stated precision?
options: The estimate is no more than $12,000.
The estimate is between $11,900 and $12,100.
The estimate exceeds $12,000 by a small amount.
The estimate is around $12,000.
answer: The estimate is around $12,000.
focusKey: coverage-hedging-and-precision-b2-1635:In the region of without an invented tolerance
explanation: 'Around' preserves an approximate amount without inventing exact limits.

An approximate center is not an upper limit.
rationales.The estimate is between $11,900 and $12,: This invents a narrow range that the analyst did not specify.
rationales.The estimate exceeds $12,000 by a small: The phrase does not say the estimate is above $12,000.
'Around' preserves an approximate amount without inventing exact limits.

sentence: Which description captures her position?
setupText: A colleague says, 'I'm inclined to recommend the smaller venue, though I haven't made up my mind.'
taskText: Which description captures her position?
text: A colleague says, 'I'm inclined to recommend the smaller venue, though I haven't made up my mind.' Which description captures her position?
options: She is required to recommend the smaller venue.
She leans toward recommending the smaller venue.
She has decided to recommend the smaller venue.
She considers the smaller venue unsuitable for a recommendation.
answer: She leans toward recommending the smaller venue.
explanation: 'Inclined to' expresses a preference that has not become a final decision.

rationales.She leans toward recommending the smalle: 'Inclined to' expresses a preference that has not become a final decision.
rationales.She is required to recommend the smaller: Inclination is a personal leaning, not an obligation.
rationales.She has decided to recommend the smaller: The second clause explicitly says her mind is not made up.
rationales.She considers the smaller venue unsuitab: This reverses the positive leaning she expresses.

sentence: Which summary keeps both parts?
setupText: A notice says, 'The discount applies primarily to off-peak journeys; selected peak-time journeys also qualify.'
taskText: Which summary keeps both parts?
text: A notice says, 'The discount applies primarily to off-peak journeys; selected peak-time journeys also qualify.' Which summary keeps both parts?
options: Only off-peak journeys qualify for the discount.
Off-peak and peak-time journeys qualify on the same basis.
The discount mainly covers off-peak travel, with some peak-time exceptions.
Peak-time journeys are increasingly likely to qualify for the discount.
answer: The discount mainly covers off-peak travel, with some peak-time exceptions.
explanation: 'Mainly' preserves the primary category while the second phrase retains the exceptions.

rationales.Only off-peak journeys qualify for the d: This removes the selected peak-time exceptions.
rationales.The discount mainly covers off-peak trav: 'Mainly' preserves the primary category while the second phrase retains the exceptions.
rationales.Off-peak and peak-time journeys qualify: The notice distinguishes the main category from selected exceptions.
rationales.Peak-time journeys are increasingly like: No trend over time is stated.

sentence: Which answer is appropriately precise?
setupText: You have two current quotations: $6,200 from Firm A and $6,750 from Firm B. You are asked which quoted price is lower.
taskText: Which answer is appropriately precise?
text: You have two current quotations: $6,200 from Firm A and $6,750 from Firm B. You are asked which quoted price is lower. Which answer is appropriately precise?
options: Firm A's quoted price is $550 lower.
Firm A may be the cheaper provider over the long term.
Firm B seems less competitive in the wider market.
Firm A is probably the better choice overall.
answer: Firm A's quoted price is $550 lower.
explanation: $6,750 minus $6,200 is $550. 'Quoted price' confines this exact comparison to the offers, without claiming lower long-term costs or better overall value.

rationales.Firm A may be the cheaper provider over: This forecasts long-term costs, which two current quotations do not establish.
rationales.Firm B seems less competitive in the wid: The question compares two quotations, not the wider market.
$6,750 minus $6,200 is $550. 'Quoted price' confines this exact comparison to the offers, without claiming lower long-term costs or better overall value.
rationales.Firm A is probably the better choice ove: A lower quoted price alone does not settle which firm is better overall.

sentence: Which revision preserves the evidence and its limits?
setupText: A draft says, 'The interviews suggest that some staff find the new process confusing.' The writer did not measure how many staff share that view.
taskText: Which revision preserves the evidence and its limits?
text: A draft says, 'The interviews suggest that some staff find the new process confusing.' The writer did not measure how many staff share that view. Which revision preserves the evidence and its limits?
options: Some staff appear to find the process confusing, based on the interviews.
The interviews show that confusion is widespread among staff.
The interviews suggest that the process confuses staff more than before.
The process is probably confusing for most staff members.
answer: Some staff appear to find the process confusing, based on the interviews.
explanation: 'Appear to' marks an inference, 'some' avoids an unmeasured proportion, and 'based on the interviews' states the evidence behind the interpretation.

rationales.The interviews show that confusion is wi: 'Widespread' adds a prevalence claim that was not measured.
rationales.The process is probably confusing for mo: 'Most' invents a majority, and the interview attribution disappears.
rationales.Some staff appear to find the process co: 'Appear to' marks an inference, 'some' avoids an unmeasured proportion, and 'based on the interviews' states the evidence behind the interpretation.

sentence: Which paraphrase keeps the limited causal claim?
setupText: The team writes, 'The improvement can be attributed in part to better training.'
taskText: Which paraphrase keeps the limited causal claim?
text: The team writes, 'The improvement can be attributed in part to better training.' Which paraphrase keeps the limited causal claim?
options: Better training was the main contributor to the improvement.
Better training may have occurred after the improvement.
Better training was one contributor to the improvement.
Part of the training improved, although the outcome stayed the same.
answer: Better training was one contributor to the improvement.
focusKey: coverage-hedging-and-precision-b2-1640:In part as a limit on causal extent
explanation: 'In part' assigns some causal contribution without treating training as the full explanation.

rationales.Better training was one contributor to t: 'In part' assigns some causal contribution without treating training as the full explanation.
rationales.Better training was the main contributor: 'In part' does not say training contributed more than other factors.
rationales.Better training may have occurred after: This changes a causal contribution into uncertainty about timing.
rationales.Part of the training improved, although: This shifts 'in part' to the training itself and removes the stated improvement.
